children: Our Bureau Bengaluru: Digital lending startup Fibe has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) for its proposed initial public offering comprising a fresh issue of up to 750 crore and an offer for sale of 40.07 million shares by existing investors.

According to its draft red herring prospectus, Fibe's major investors including TPG's The Rise Fund, Norwest Venture Partners, Chiratae Ventures, Piramal Finance and Eight Roads Ventures are selling shares as part of the public offering.

The Pune-based company plans to invest 562.6 crore from the fresh proceeds in EarlySalary Services Pvt Ltd (ESPL), its non-banking financial company arm, to augment its capital base and support onward lending. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2015 by Akshay Mehrotra and Ashish Goyal, Fibe was previously known as EarlySalary. It started as a small-ticket, short-duration personal loan provider and has since expanded into longer-tenure unsecured personal loans and purpose-linked financing across healthcare, education, insurance and other consumption categories.

title: Fibe Gets Sebi Approval for 750-cr IPO
